---
title: "Posterior profiles on multiple criteria"
subtitle: "4.1 · after the postrank vignette m2 and theory book, ch. 12"
description: "Criterion-specific scales, orderings and pairwise direction probabilities for common units."
---

The same units can have different posterior orderings on different criteria. Each panel retains its criterion's
measurement scale, posterior means and marginal intervals. Connecting lines identify units across the separate
orders, and the pair display gives the error probability of a proposed direction on each criterion. Aligning rows
by unit makes their profiles comparable without constructing a composite score. The examples distinguish
opposition between preferred directions from uncertainty within a criterion, and show the effect of reversing the
substantive orientation of one target.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Thirty sites.** There are 397 opposing pairs among 435 pairs. The highest posterior mean belongs to a different
  site on each criterion. Alignment by unit labels displays each unit's criterion-specific profiles.
- **Six sites, B–C.** The error of stating B above C is .007 on score A and .961 on score B. The complete list has
  3 opposing pairs. A very likely direction on one criterion can be very unlikely on another.
- **Six sites, B–D.** The errors are .002 on score A and .760 on score B. Matching row labels leaves each
  criterion’s scale intact; it does not turn the scores into one composite.
- **Reverse score B.** Lower score B now means higher priority. The error of stating B above C on the oriented
  score becomes .039. The supplied information stays the same; the substantive direction of the target changes.
- **Wider intervals.** The marginal level becomes 95%, while the 397 opposing pairs stay the same. Interval level
  changes the displayed uncertainty bands, not the supplied posterior probabilities or mean orders.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
For the fictional six sites, score A is standardised reading growth and score B a standardised family-engagement
index; higher values mean higher visit priority by default. Grades would decide only the order of
practice-documentation visits, with no funding consequence. These are supplied synthetic normal laws: intervals
are marginal, not simultaneous, and thirty-site marginal releases do not supply a composite or sampled joint state.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
pr_tutorial$two$e["B", "C", ]
pr_tutorial$two$e["B", "D", ]
```
:::
